text:
Sam R.: FYI customer @Acme ran into a blocker building our Go SDK: CI fails with checksum mismatch + repeated 403s from their goproxy when resolving a tagged release after a `replace` was added.
Alex P.: ugh, any logs/commands they ran?
Sam R.: They sent repro steps.
Sam R.: 1) clone repo
Sam R.: 2) in module A go.mod they have `replace github.com/redwood/dep => ../dep-local` in local dev, but in CI they switched to `replace github.com/redwood/dep => github.com/fork/dep v2.0.1`
Sam R.: 3) `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go build ./...` in CI
Sam R.: CI output: ```
verifying github.com/fork/dep@v2.0.1: checksum mismatch
	downloaded: h1:abcdef...
	go.sum:    h1:012345...
``` 
Sam R.: Then subsequent attempts return 403 from goproxy.company.com when fetching the zip for the tag (their proxy sits in front of goproxy)
Jordan L.: Do they use a private proxy that rejects certain zip contents? 403 suggests auth or proxy ACL.
Maria K.: They said it started after the maintainer force-pushed and re-tagged v2.0.1 last week.
Alex P.: Force-pushing a tag invalidates the module zip; go.sum will mismatch. If their proxy caches the old zip and then tries to fetch the new one, mismatches/403s can happen.
Sam R.: Repro I ran locally by mimic: `git tag -f v2.0.1 && git push --force origin refs/tags/v2.0.1` then `go clean -modcache` then `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go get github.com/fork/dep@v2.0.1` -> checksum mismatch.
Jordan L.: Workarounds: 1) pin to pseudo-version `github.com/fork/dep v0.0.0-20230201123456-abcdef123456` 2) use commit hash instead of tag, 3) vendor the dep.
Maria K.: Customer tried `go clean -modcache` and `rm -rf $GOMODCACHE` but their CI proxy still served the old zip and returned 403 when backing to origin.
Alex P.: For immediate unblock we suggested changing the replace to point at the commit hash: `replace github.com/redwood/dep => github.com/fork/dep v0.0.0-...-abcdef123456` and purge their proxy cache for that path.
Sam R.: They applied the hack and CI greened.
Jordan L.: Long term: recommend the fork maintainer avoid force-pushing tags. Also add a support doc about tag force-push consequences and mitigation steps for customers using private proxies.
Maria K.: Action items:
- Alex: propose small template message for customers explaining cause + immediate workarounds (commit pin, vendor, or use pseudo-version).
- Jordan: check if our SDK release pipeline ever uses non-immutable tags; make sure we sign/annotate tags.
- Sam: offer to help the customer purge their proxy cache or route around it.
Alex P.: I'll draft the support template and a short FAQ entry.
Jordan L.: I'll open an infra issue for release pipeline tag hygiene.
ci-bot: Deployed support-doc patch draft at https://confluence.redwood/sd/tag-forcepush-guidance (draft) :memo:
Sam R.: thanks, folks. I'll follow up with the customer and paste the fix + commands I ran.
Sam R.: (cc @Maria K. will coordinate purge with them)
Maria K.: :thumbsup:
